quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lane markings mean?

options.text: No one can pass.
Both lanes can pass.
The right lane can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow markings separate lanes with traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass in either direction.

questions.question: Which statement is true about medications and driving?

options.text: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter medicines are safe for driving if you take the right amount.
Any medicine prescribed by a doctor is safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medicines—prescription or over-the-counter—can affect your driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy and impair your ability to drive. You must know how your medicines affect you before driving.

questions.question: You are following a large truck on the freeway. How should you drive?

options.text: Stay close behind the truck in bad weather so you can see ahead.
Stay farther back than you would with a regular car.
Stay one car length behind so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back than you would with a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely, the truck driver cannot see you in their mirrors. You lose your safety space if they stop suddenly. Always stay farther back from trucks than from regular cars.

questions.question: What risk does fatigue increase?

options.text: Missing an exit.
Being late.
Falling asleep and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue causes mistakes in speed and distance judgment. It slows your decisions and increases crash risk. You can fall asleep at the wheel and crash, hurting yourself or others.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Watch for traffic merging from the right.
Merge right.
Turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for traffic merging from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns you that traffic will merge into your lane from the right.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from the left.
You can pass from the right.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines show traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid lines mean no passing is allowed from either side.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is not unsafe.
Driving too slowly can be dangerous on some highways.
Speed does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly can be dangerous on some highways.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly frustrates other drivers and can cause dangerous passing attempts. Drive with traffic flow, within the legal speed limit.

questions.question: How can you help the driver behind you stay a safe distance away?

options.text: Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
Maintain a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a steady speed.
questions.explanation: Keep a steady speed to help the driver behind you stay at a safe distance. Signal your turns, lane changes, and slowdowns in advance.

questions.question: As you drive faster, what is important to do?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look far ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: As speed increases, stopping distance increases. Look far ahead at higher speeds so you have space to react safely to dangers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Divided highway.
Railroad warning.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you a divided highway is starting ahead.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses traction because of water on the road, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to get better traction.
Press the brakes hard to stop your vehicle from sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: When driving in heavy rain at speeds as low as 30 mph, your tires may lose contact with the road. The tires ride on a layer of water instead. This is called hydroplaning. If this happens, slow down gradually and do not use the brakes.

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, which lane should you start from?

options.text: Any lane, as long as it is safe.
The lane closest to the left curb.
The center lane of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, start your turn from the far left lane.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a safe driving practice on the interstate?

options.text: Slower traffic stays in the right lane.
Change lanes without signaling.
If you miss your exit, go to the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes without signaling.
questions.explanation: Always signal when you move your vehicle left or right. Stay in the right lane if you are driving slower than other traffic on the interstate. It is illegal to back up or make a U-turn on interstate highways. If you miss your exit, continue to the next exit.

questions.question: When are collisions more likely to happen?

options.text: When all vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.
When one lane of traffic is faster than other lanes.
When one vehicle is traveling much faster or slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When one vehicle is traveling much faster or slower than other traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions are more likely when one driver goes faster or slower than other vehicles on the road. Driving faster than traffic increases your risk of a collision. Driving slower than traffic is also dangerous because it can cause rear-end collisions or force other drivers to swerve to avoid you.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a construction zone?

options.text: Stop to watch the workers.
Drive closer to the car in front of you.
Pass through carefully and do not stare at the construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass through carefully and do not stare at the construction.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at the construction. Staring at the construction causes traffic to back up. Keep your focus on driving safely through the zone.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signals?

options.text: Only when leaving the curb.
Only when pulling up to the curb.
When pulling up to the curb and when leaving the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling up to the curb and when leaving the curb.
questions.explanation: You should signal both when you pull up to a curb and when you leave a curb.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle using its flashing lights, what must you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, pull over to the right edge of the road and stop. Park parallel to the curb. On one-way streets, drive toward the nearest road edge.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, what should you do with your headlights?

options.text: Keep them on low beam.
Use high beam until you are within 10 feet of the car ahead.
Use your high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep them on low beam.
questions.explanation: Use high beam headlights only when driving in rural areas with no other cars nearby. Switch to low beam when you are following another vehicle closely.

questions.question: You want to pass a motorcycle. What must you do?

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small and doesn't use all of the lane.
Honk your horn to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder.
Keep your entire vehicle in the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your entire vehicle in the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: When passing a motorcycle, give it a full lane. Never share a lane with a motorcycle. If you return to the original lane too soon, the motorcycle may have to swerve right into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, when can you proceed in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
When the light changes to green.
When you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: If you are in a lane with a green arrow, you can go in the direction of the arrow when the road is clear. This is true whether the arrow appears alone or with another signal.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you about a steep hill coming up. Slow down and be ready to use your brakes to avoid crashes and damage.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.
Passing cars.
No one in particular.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: When you turn left, you must yield to all vehicles coming toward you from the opposite direction. This includes bicycles and motorcycles.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should check your mirrors and:

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your traffic lane.
Glance over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Glance over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check behind you. Make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Also check that other drivers are not moving into the same spot.

questions.question: If bad weather makes it hard to see, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get off the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: In bad weather or darkness, stay farther back from the car in front of you. This gives you more time to react to hazards you may not see.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars on the right move first.
You have the right-of-way.
Let cross traffic pass before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let cross traffic pass before proceeding.
questions.explanation: This sign means you must yield. Slow down and let vehicles and pedestrians cross in front of you before you go. Stop if you need to.
